title: eval-harness: add CI prompt-regression gating + metrics export for quality gating
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: prevent prompt-set regressions from reaching production by adding a GitHub Actions CI gate that runs a lightweight eval-harness sweep against a maintained set of prompt tests and fails the PR if quality thresholds drop. This PR also adds an exporter to surface eval metrics to Redwood Console so quality gates can be centrally observed and tuned.

What this changes (single-string description):
- Adds .github/workflows/eval-ci.yml: a scheduled and PR-triggered workflow that starts a GPU-backed runner when necessary, runs a subset of the regression prompt-sets, and posts results as a check. The workflow uses self-hosted labels and falls back to a CPU-only path for CI quotas.
- New tools/eval_ci_runner.py: lightweight runner that loads prompt sets, runs batch evaluation with timeouts, computes per-prompt metrics (EM, F1, ROUGE-L for NLG sets), and exits non-zero when configured thresholds are violated.
- eval-config/prompt_sets.yml: canonical list of guarded prompt sets + thresholds (per-prompt and aggregate pass rates).
- integrations/console_metrics_exporter.py: ships a minimal metrics payload (eval run id, prompt set, pass/fail, top-level metrics) to observability; includes retries and backoff.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for runner logic, an integration test that mocks the observability endpoint, and documentation in docs/eval-harness/ci.md describing how to add new prompt sets and tune thresholds.

Behavior notes:
- CI gating is opt-in for repositories via a repo-level config (eval-config/ci_enabled: true). For the monorepo we enabled gating on the redwood/serving and redwood/eval-harness folders only to limit runtime cost.
- The runner has a retry strategy for transient failures (GPU allocation/timeouts). The workflow will surface an informational check on first failure and auto-rerun once before marking the job failed to reduce flakes.

Why:
- Recent regressions in prompt-based behavior were only detected post-merge during canary; moving detection earlier reduces rollback churn and improves confidence for model and infra changes.

Testing performed:
- Local smoke runs using the CPU fallback path.
- End-to-end runs on a self-hosted GPU runner (3 consecutive runs) to validate metrics and exporter.
- CI: the first push hit a transient allocation failure; after adding the retry and increasing timeout the workflow passes in subsequent run.

Security and cost: metrics payloads avoid sending raw prompt text; only hashed prompt IDs and aggregated metrics are exported. The exporter uses the existing service account with restricted scope.

Rollout plan: gated by feature flag. We will enable for critical folders first, monitor false positives for two weeks, then expand.

Integrations: add Console metrics exporter and retries

Adds a GitHub Actions workflow, a lightweight eval CI runner, prompt set config and a metrics exporter to Redwood Console.

Closes ENG-4213.
release_notes:
- Add eval-harness CI gating workflow to catch prompt-set regressions early.
- Export eval metrics to Console for quality gating and observability.
- New config file for guarded prompt sets and thresholds.
